spec.functions: dav1d_splat_mv_rvv(refmvs_block **rr, const refmvs_block *rmv, int bx4, int bw4, int bh4)
spec.formula: for each of bh4 rows: r = rr[row] + bx4; r[x] = *rmv for 0 <= x < bw4 (refmvs_block is a packed 12-byte struct, 4-byte aligned)
spec.domain: bw4 in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}; 1 <= bh4 <= 32; bx4 a multiple of bw4; row pointers are independent (read each rr[row]: rows are not at a fixed stride); rmv 4-byte aligned; row bases 4-byte aligned (64 in practice)
width_bounds: pure data movement: every byte written is a byte of *rmv
nothing outside r[0 .. bw4-1] of each of the bh4 rows may change
every VLEN from 128 to 1024; plain RVV 1.0 plus Zba/Zbb (the X280 has no Zbs)

regimes.bench: checkasm --bench: one cell per width, splat_mv_w1 .. splat_mv_w32, over h from max(w/4,1) to min(4w,32)
regimes.check: checkasm: every width, h from max(w/4,1) to min(4w,32), random bx4 offsets (multiples of w), random block contents

candidates.title: Build the repeated 12-byte pattern once per call
candidates.application: one vector register group holding *rmv repeated (vle32 of 3 words + vrgather with a precomputed i%3 index, or vslideup doubling), built before the row loop
candidates.expected_gain: the per-row work is only stores
preconditions: the pattern must start at the first byte of each row's r + bx4

candidates.title: One unit-stride store per row
candidates.application: each row is a contiguous 12*bw4 bytes: store it with one vse8/vse32 when VLMAX allows (VLEN 512, e8 m8 = 512 bytes >= 384), else a short strip loop

candidates.title: Dispatch on bw4 to a path per width
candidates.application: a jump table or branch on bw4 (6 sizes) with a straight-line path per width, as arm64/x86 do
candidates.expected_gain: no per-row vl computation; small widths avoid vector setup
preconditions: dispatch only on bw4, never on data

candidates.title: Scalar stores for the narrowest widths
candidates.application: bw4 = 1 or 2 (12 or 24 bytes): scalar sd/sw from three or six registers may beat vector setup
candidates.expected_gain: lower fixed cost on w1/w2 cells
preconditions: the hot path must stay vector for the wide cells (contract: no scalar port)
sources: arm64 10/20 paths use one 8-byte + one 4-byte store

candidates.title: Unroll rows
candidates.application: 2-4 rows per iteration: load the next row pointers early, issue stores back to back
candidates.expected_gain: hides the pointer-load latency on the in-order X280

candidates.application: vtype and vl are the same for every row: set them once
candidates.expected_gain: no vsetvli in the row loop

candidates.application: LMUL 8 so one store covers a whole row
candidates.expected_gain: fewer stores per row at small VLEN

candidates.application: build the pattern with slides instead of vrgather (gather cost grows with LMUL on the X280)
ta,ma: tail elements of the pattern register are dead
